S1 — BLOCKING (P2): alignment-sensitive contact effects replace a printed complement predicate with a narrower alignment category.
Invariant/authority: USER's faithful-or-absent decision, owning .19.4.5 DESIGN/AC1/AC3, ADR 0020 source fidelity and the printed talisman descriptions require every positively typed effect to retain the printed affected-creature predicate exactly, or be withheld with its verbatim adjudicated span. This applies to the whole effects population, including unchanged pre-existing siblings; it is not a requirement to execute them or create a contract layer. Profile rules-clause-complete; owner .19.4.5.

Confirmed membership:
1. magic-item:talisman-of-pure-good / m7-pure-good-alignment-contact.result. packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/magicItemCurses.ts:652; emitted packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json:138512. Typed result: "neutral creature takes 6d6 radiant; evil creature takes 8d6 radiant".
2. magic-item:talisman-of-ultimate-evil / m7-ultimate-evil-alignment-contact.result. Same producer :713; records.json:139050. Typed result: "neutral creature takes 6d6 necrotic; good creature takes 8d6 necrotic".

Printed authority for BOTH (p.247; description at records.json:138469 and :139007): "A creature that is neither good nor evil in alignment" takes the corresponding 6d6 contact damage, again at end of a turn holding/carrying it. rule:alignment defines neutral as an alignment category; rule:alignment-in-the-multiverse and rule:monsters-alignment expressly distinguish unaligned creatures, which have NO alignment. The source predicates "neither good nor evil" and "neutral" therefore cannot be substituted as the same recipient set. This is a defined source distinction, not a guessed meaning for an undefined marker such as active or eligible.

Distinguishing scenario for each talisman: an unaligned wolf (creature:wolf) touches it, or carries it at turn end. It is neither good nor evil, but is not a creature of neutral alignment. The printed complement includes that state; the typed neutral branch does not state it. No other effect, operation or clause representation supplies the missing recipient alternative; the two contact readiness clauses merely bind this result and remain engine-pending. Consequence is a narrower model-facing damage claim, not an alleged currently executing green-operation defect. Even if the DM must interpret a source edge case, the typed projection must preserve the source wording rather than resolve it by silently substituting an alignment category.

Sibling/state-space analysis: read all alignment-sensitive typed effects (including both talismans' spell bonuses, fissures and eligibility; Candle matching alignment; Archmagi color/alignment; Mind Shielding) and all parent/variant effects. Varied good/evil, lawful-neutral/neutral/chaotic-neutral, unaligned, touch versus holding/carrying at turn end, and contact victim versus attuned bearer. Archmagi explicitly prints neutral for gray and Candle explicitly prints matching alignment; neither is this complement-to-category loss. The talisman +2 roll-scope repairs are correct and are not reopened. Exactly two confirmed effect carriers are batched here.

Closure: through the curated producer, make BOTH contact result branches retain "a creature that is neither good nor evil in alignment" and the correct damage/event alternatives, or withhold the contact claims with complete verbatim spans. Preserve the good/evil 8d6 branches, contact/turn-end events and existing bonus/fissure predicates. Regenerate pack/inventory and reconcile registry evidence. Extend existing source-qualification evidence with proportionate GENERALIZED complement-versus-category protection anchored to the printed predicates, retaining the unaligned distinguishing case and both source-backed members. Cheap source assertions suffice; no per-ability contract, new executor or universal natural-language proof. Material rules-semantic repair requires fresh full review at its regenerated exact head.
